def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """For each candidate: count of its channel partners whose current domain is a singleton strictly inside this candidate's range-adjacency — measures propagation depth through chains, normalised by partner count."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom = domain.astype(np.float64)
    dsize = dom.sum(axis=1)  # (k,)

    # singleton partners: partners with domain size exactly 1
    partner_single = (dsize == 1.0).astype(np.float64)  # (k,)
    # which depth each singleton partner is pinned to
    single_depth = np.argmax(dom, axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # (k,) valid where singleton

    # channel masks
    apart_mask = (links == 1).astype(np.float64)
    close_mask = (links == 2).astype(np.float64)

    # For each candidate i and each of its own feasible depths v, count partners j
    # that are singletons and whose pinned depth is COMPATIBLE with v.
    # apart: |v - pinned_j| > 0 ; close: |v - pinned_j| <= 1
    v = np.arange(4).astype(np.float64)
    diff = np.abs(v[:, None] - single_depth[None, :])  # (4, k)
    apart_ok = (diff > 0.5).astype(np.float64)  # (4,k)
    close_ok = (diff < 1.5).astype(np.float64)

    # restrict to actual singleton partners
    single_mask = (dsize == 1.0)[None, :]  # (1,k)
    apart_ok = apart_ok * single_mask
    close_ok = close_ok * single_mask

    # count compatible singleton partners per own depth
    apart_cnt = apart_mask @ apart_ok.T  # (k,4)
    close_cnt = close_mask @ close_ok.T  # (k,4)

    # total singleton channel partners per candidate
    total_single = apart_mask @ single_mask[0] + close_mask @ single_mask[0]  # (k,)

    # for each candidate: average over feasible depths of the fraction of singleton
    # partners that are compatible. High = this candidate's remaining depths are
    # consistent with already-pinned neighbours (safe to branch, likely propagation).
    per_depth = np.where(dsize[:, None] > 0, (apart_cnt + close_cnt) / np.maximum(total_single[:, None], 1.0), 0.0)
    frac = (per_depth * dom).sum(axis=1) / np.maximum(dsize, 1.0)

    # zero out candidates with no singleton partners (no signal)
    frac = np.where(total_single > 0, frac, 0.0)
    return np.clip(frac, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Max tightness 1/(1+max(slack_lo,0)+max(slack_hi,0)) over the candidate's basins with at most 2 open members, 0 if none."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    if B == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # feasible depths per candidate: (k, 4) bool -> min/max feasible depth
    depths = np.arange(4, dtype=float)
    has = domain.astype(bool)
    big = 1e6
    dmin = np.where(has, depths[None, :], big).min(axis=1)   # (k,)
    dmax = np.where(has, depths[None, :], -big).max(axis=1)  # (k,)

    # open members of each basin are exactly the candidates (all unassigned pools)
    member = basins.astype(bool)                              # (k, B)
    open_count = basin_open.astype(float)                     # (B,)
    qualifies = open_count <= 2                               # (B,)

    # sum of min/max feasible depth over open members of each basin
    sum_min = member.T.astype(float) @ dmin                   # (B,)
    sum_max = member.T.astype(float) @ dmax                   # (B,)

    rest = basin_rest.astype(float)                           # (B,)
    slack_lo = rest - sum_min
    slack_hi = sum_max - rest
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.maximum(slack_lo, 0.0) + np.maximum(slack_hi, 0.0))  # (B,)
    tight = np.where(qualifies, tight, 0.0)

    # max tightness over qualifying basins per candidate
    vals = np.where(member, tight[None, :], 0.0).max(axis=1)  # (k,)
    return vals

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Mean over a candidate's feasible depths of the minimum (supply - demand) census slack after pinning it to that depth, divided by max(k,1)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    S = domain.sum(axis=0).astype(np.float64)          # (4,) supply per depth
    D = census_left.astype(np.float64)                 # (4,) demand per depth
    base = S - D                                       # (4,) slack before pinning
    # For candidate i pinned to depth d: supply'_t = S[t] - domain[i,t] + (t==d)
    #                                  demand'_t = D[t] - (t==d)
    # slack_t = base[t] - domain[i,t] + 2*(t==d)
    # min over t of slack_t = min( min_{t!=d}(base[t]-domain[i,t]), base[d]-domain[i,d]+2 )
    # Compute per (i,d) the min over t.
    # slack matrix: shape (k, 4, 4) would be large; do it via two parts.
    # part A: min over t of (base[t] - domain[i,t])  -> (k,)
    slack_no_pin = base[None, :] - domain.astype(np.float64)   # (k,4)
    min_all = slack_no_pin.min(axis=1)                          # (k,)
    # For pinned depth d, the d-th term becomes base[d]-domain[i,d]+2, others unchanged.
    # min over t = min( min over t!=d, pinned_d_term )
    # We need min over t!=d of slack_no_pin[i,t]. Compute by masking.
    # Use a large value for the d-th entry to get min over t!=d.
    big = 1e9
    masked = np.where(domain, slack_no_pin, big)                # only feasible depths matter for t? 
    # Actually t ranges over all 4 depths regardless of domain[i,t]; domain[i,t] is 0/1.
    # slack_no_pin already uses domain[i,t] (0 or 1). So min over t!=d uses all t.
    # Build min over t!=d:
    # For each d, set column d to big and take min.
    # Vectorised: for each candidate, for each feasible d.
    # We'll compute per feasible (i,d).
    vals = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    counts = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    for d in range(4):
        feas = domain[:, d]
        if not np.any(feas):
            continue
        # min over t != d
        col = slack_no_pin.copy()
        col[:, d] = big
        min_other = col.min(axis=1)                             # (k,)
        pinned_term = base[d] - domain[:, d].astype(np.float64) + 2.0
        slack_d = np.minimum(min_other, pinned_term)            # (k,)
        vals += np.where(feas, slack_d, 0.0)
        counts += feas.astype(np.float64)
    counts = np.maximum(counts, 1.0)
    out = (vals / counts) / max(k, 1)
    return out

What separates pools early is how close the census comes to being unsatisfiable *after* the depth is taken, i.e. the minimum supply-minus-demand slack over depths. A continuous quantity, so it ranks candidates everywhere instead of only at the rare violations.

For each candidate i and each feasible depth d: supply'_t = S[t] - domain[i,t] + (t==d), demand'_t = D[t] - (t==d), slack = min over t of (supply'_t - demand'_t). Value = mean of slack over the candidate's feasible depths, divided by max(k, 1).

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Basin slack tightness recomputed as the fraction of basin total that is actually forced: how much of the basin's remaining total is pinned by the sum of open members' minimum feasible depths, averaged (weighted by tightness) over the basins a candidate belongs to."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    M = basins.astype(float)
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)

    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min          # (B,)
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max          # (B,)
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)  # (B,)
    spread = slo + shi               # (B,) total slack

    # how much of the basin total is pinned: fraction of remaining rest that the
    # minimum feasible sum already accounts for, near 1 means little freedom left.
    rest = np.maximum(basin_rest.astype(float), 0.0)
    pinned = min_sum / np.maximum(rest, 1e-6)          # (B,)
    pinned = np.clip(pinned, 0.0, 1.0)

    # combine: pinned fraction amplified by tightness -> a basin that is both
    # tightly pinned and low-slack is a strong decision point.
    score_b = pinned * tight                            # (B,)

    # candidates in no basin get 0; candidates with several basins take the max
    masked = np.where(basins, score_b[None, :], -1.0)
    best = masked.max(axis=1)
    out = np.where(basins.any(axis=1), best, 0.0)

    # spread penalty: candidates in basins with huge slack are less decisive
    spread_b = 1.0 / (1.0 + spread)
    masked_s = np.where(basins, spread_b[None, :], -1.0)
    best_s = masked_s.max(axis=1)
    out = out * np.where(basins.any(axis=1), best_s, 1.0)

    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Basin slack tightness recomputed as the fraction of basin total that is actually forced: how much of the basin's remaining total is pinned by the sum of open members' minimum feasible depths, averaged (weighted by tightness) over the basins a candidate belongs to.

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """For each candidate: basin-derived stranding risk aggregated over ALL its basins (max, not just tightest), weighted by slack ratio and by how much of the basin's open mass the candidate controls — negative when branching risks stranding a basin."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom_size = np.maximum(domain.sum(axis=1).astype(float), 1.0)
    M = basins.astype(float)                      # (k,B)
    in_basin = basins                              # (k,B)
    B = basins.shape[1]

    # Per-basin slack geometry from current domains (same family as f007)
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min                        # (B,)
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max                        # (B,)
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)    # (B,)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)    # (B,)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)                # (B,)

    open_cnt = basin_open.astype(float)            # (B,)
    others = np.maximum(open_cnt[None, :] - M, 0.0)  # (k,B) other open members

    # For each candidate-depth, check whether the remaining open members can
    # still cover the residual -> basin not stranded.
    rest_b = basin_rest[None, :, None]             # (1,B,1)
    v = np.arange(4)[None, None, :]                # (1,1,4)
    residual = rest_b - v                          # (1,B,4)
    oth = others[:, :, None]                       # (k,B,1)
    lo = np.maximum(residual - 3.0 * oth, 0.0)
    hi = np.minimum(residual, 3.0 * oth)
    ok = (residual >= lo - 1e-9) & (residual <= hi + 1e-9) & (residual >= 0.0)

    own_feas = domain[:, None, :].astype(bool)     # (k,1,4)
    has_other = (others > 0)[:, :, None]           # (k,B,1)
    bad = own_feas & (~ok) & has_other             # (k,B,4)
    n_bad = bad.sum(axis=2).astype(float)          # (k,B)
    frac_b = np.where(in_basin, n_bad / dom_size[:, None], 0.0)  # (k,B)

    # New: how much of the basin's open mass this candidate controls.
    # More open members -> candidate controls a smaller share -> less leverage on strandings.
    share = np.where(in_basin, 1.0 / np.maximum(open_cnt[None, :], 1.0), 0.0)  # (k,B)

    # Emphasise basins that are BOTH tight in slack AND mostly-open (still undecided,
    # so a wrong branch here is costly and hard to repair) — slack-derived, not just 1/(1+slack).
    slack = slo + shi                              # (B,)
    emphasis = (tight / (1.0 + slack))[None, :]    # (B,), sharper on very tight basins

    # Aggregate over ALL basins with a smooth max (log-sum-exp) instead of hard max,
    # so multiple near-stranding basins compound rather than being ignored.
    risks = frac_b * share * emphasis              # (k,B)
    risks = np.where(in_basin, risks, 0.0)
    scale = np.maximum(risks.max(axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-6)
    # temperature-free softmax over normalized basin risks -> concentrates on worst basin
    z = risks / scale
    lse = np.log(np.exp(z).sum(axis=1) + 1e-9) - np.log(np.maximum(in_basin.sum(axis=1), 1))
    agg = scale[:, 0] * lse

    # Also fold in the channel side: candidates whose feasible depths conflict with
    # many assigned channel partners are bad places to branch (more propagation work).
    diff = np.abs(np.arange(4)[:, None] - np.arange(4)[None, :])
    apart_ok = (diff > 0).astype(float)
    close_ok = (diff <= 1).astype(float)
    domf = domain.astype(float)
    comp_a = domf @ apart_ok.T                     # (k,4)
    comp_c = domf @ close_ok.T
    apart_m = (links == 1).astype(float)
    close_m = (links == 2).astype(float)
    partner_comp = apart_m @ comp_a + close_m @ comp_c   # (k,4)
    npart = apart_m.sum(1) + close_m.sum(1)
    # weighted by how much census slack is present per depth (rare depths matter more)
    tot = float(max(census_left.sum(), 1))
    scarcity = (tot - census_left.astype(float)) / tot
    chan_score = (partner_comp * domf * scarcity[None, :]).sum(1) / np.maximum(
        np.maximum(npart, 1) * dom_size, 1e-6)

    out = -(agg + 0.5 * chan_score)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: For each candidate: basin-derived stranding risk aggregated over ALL its basins (max, not just tightest), weighted by slack ratio and by how much of the basin's open mass the candidate controls — negative when branching risks stranding a basin.

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """For each candidate: the count of its feasible depths that leave at least one basin it belongs to with a residual that NO assignment of the other open members could reach even allowing them their full [0,3] range (hard-infeasible stranding), weighted by inverse basin openness (small basins dominate), minus a bonus for candidates whose basins are close to fully pinned."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom_size = domain.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    safe_size = np.where(dom_size > 0, dom_size, 1.0)

    M = basins.astype(float)                          # (k,B)
    open_cnt = basin_open.astype(float)               # (B,)
    rest_b = basin_rest[None, :]                      # (1,B)

    # hard-infeasible check: residual must be coverable by `others` members each in [0,3]
    others = np.maximum(open_cnt[None, :] - M, 0.0)   # (k,B)
    v = np.arange(4)[None, None, :]                   # (1,1,4)
    residual = rest_b[:, :, None] - v                 # (1,B,4)

    lo = np.maximum(residual - 3.0 * others[:, :, None], 0.0)
    hi = np.minimum(residual, 3.0 * others[:, :, None])
    hard_ok = (residual >= lo - 1e-9) & (residual <= hi + 1e-9) & (residual >= -1e-9)

    own_feas = domain[:, None, :].astype(bool)        # (k,1,4)
    has_other = (others > 0)[:, :, None]              # (k,B,1)
    bad = own_feas & (~hard_ok) & has_other           # (k,B,4)
    n_bad_b = bad.sum(axis=2).astype(float)           # (k,B)

    # weight: small basins dominate; tightness of slack from domain ranges
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)                   # (B,)
    inv_open = 1.0 / np.maximum(open_cnt, 1.0)        # (B,)

    w_b = tight * inv_open                            # (B,)
    frac_b = np.where(basins, n_bad_b / safe_size[:, None], 0.0)
    stranding = (frac_b * w_b[None, :]).sum(axis=1)

    # bonus: fraction of each candidate's basins that are fully pinned (every open
    # member has a singleton domain) — a strong sign the candidate is nearly forced,
    # and picking it resolves several basins at once.
    pinned_member = (dom_size <= 1.0).astype(float)   # (k,)
    pinned_cnt = (M * pinned_member[:, None]).sum(axis=0)  # (B,)
    fully_pinned = ((pinned_cnt >= open_cnt) & (open_cnt > 0)).astype(float)  # (B,)
    basin_count = np.maximum(M.sum(axis=1), 1.0)
    pin_frac = (M * fully_pinned[None, :]).sum(axis=1) / basin_count  # (k,)

    out = -stranding + 0.5 * pin_frac
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Per candidate: the reduction in total basin-domain entropy (over depths) that branching on it would produce, weighted by basin tightness; high when the candidate is the most entropy-reducing hinge of its tight basins."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom = domain.astype(np.float64)
    M = basins.astype(np.float64)
    B = basins.shape[1]

    # per-depth count of open members able to take each depth, per basin: (B,4)
    cnt = M.T @ dom  # (B,4)

    # entropy of a basin's depth-availability distribution: use counts as unnormalised
    # deficit = how "peaked" each basin is (low entropy => few options => constrain early)
    s = cnt.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)  # (B,1)
    p = cnt / np.maximum(s, 1.0)        # (B,4)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        ent = -(p * np.log(p + 1e-12)).sum(axis=1)  # (B,)
    ent = np.where(s[:, 0] > 0, ent, 0.0)
    max_ent = math.log(4.0)
    peak = 1.0 - ent / max_ent  # (B,): 0=uniform, 1=single option

    # basin tightness (as elsewhere): 1/(1+slack)
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(np.float64)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(np.float64)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)  # (B,)

    # how much does this candidate concentrate its basin's distributions?
    # candidate contributes dom[i,d] to cnt[b,d]; removing it leaves (cnt[b,d]-dom[i,d])
    # measure entropy drop when the candidate is fixed to each of its feasible depths, averaged
    # then combine with peak/tight, take the max over the candidate's basins.
    # (k,B,4): count after candidate removed & fixed at depth v
    dom_rem = (cnt[None, :, :] - M[:, :, None] * dom[:, None, :])  # (k,B,4)
    dom_rem = np.maximum(dom_rem, 0.0)
    s_rem = dom_rem.sum(axis=2, keepdims=True)
    p_rem = dom_rem / np.maximum(s_rem, 1.0)
    with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
        ent_rem = -(p_rem * np.log(p_rem + 1e-12)).sum(axis=2)  # (k,B)
    ent_rem = np.where(s_rem[:, :, 0] > 0, ent_rem, 0.0)
    # entropy drop relative to full entropy (only meaningful where basin has other open members)
    drop = (ent[None, :] - ent_rem) / max_ent  # (k,B)
    drop = np.maximum(drop, 0.0)

    # candidate's own feasible-depth mass (fraction of its domain), scales by its freedom
    fea = dom.sum(axis=1) / 4.0  # (k,)
    weight = (tight * (0.5 + peak))[None, :]  # (B,)
    per_basin = drop * weight
    in_b = basins
    masked = np.where(in_b, per_basin, 0.0)
    best = masked.max(axis=1)
    out = best * fea
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Per candidate: the reduction in total basin-domain entropy (over depths) that branching on it would produce, weighted by basin tightness; high when the candidate is the most entropy-reducing hinge of its tight basins.

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Max over the candidate's basins of the best-case (over feasible depths) post-pin slack tightness 1/(1+slo+shi)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    if basins.shape[1] == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # feasible depths per candidate
    feas = domain.astype(bool)  # (k,4)
    # dmin[j] = smallest feasible depth, dmax[j] = largest feasible depth
    idx = np.arange(4)
    big = 4
    dmin = np.where(feas, idx[None, :], big).min(axis=1)          # (k,)
    dmax = np.where(feas, idx[None, :], -1).max(axis=1)           # (k,)
    dmin = np.where(dmin == big, 0, dmin)
    dmax = np.where(dmax < 0, 0, dmax)

    B = basins.shape[1]
    bmask = basins.astype(bool)                                   # (k,B)

    # sums over open members of each basin (open members are exactly the candidates)
    Smin = (bmask * dmin[:, None]).sum(axis=0)                    # (B,)
    Smax = (bmask * dmax[:, None]).sum(axis=0)                    # (B,)

    # per candidate-basin: Smin_b - dmin[i], Smax_b - dmax[i]
    Smin_excl = Smin[None, :] - dmin[:, None]                     # (k,B)
    Smax_excl = Smax[None, :] - dmax[:, None]                     # (k,B)
    rest = basin_rest[None, :]                                    # (1,B)

    # for each feasible depth v: rest' = rest - v
    v = idx.astype(float)                                         # (4,)
    restp = rest[:, :, None] - v[None, None, :]                   # (1,B,4) -> broadcast (k,B,4)
    restp = np.broadcast_to(restp, (k, B, 4))

    slo = np.maximum(0.0, Smin_excl[:, :, None] - restp)          # (k,B,4)
    shi = np.maximum(0.0, restp - Smax_excl[:, :, None])          # (k,B,4)
    t = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)                                   # (k,B,4)

    # mask non-feasible depths
    t = np.where(feas[:, None, :], t, -np.inf)                    # (k,B,4)
    t_b = t.max(axis=2)                                           # (k,B) best over depths
    t_b = np.where(bmask, t_b, -np.inf)                           # only basins of i
    val = t_b.max(axis=1)                                         # (k,)
    val = np.where(np.isfinite(val), val, 0.0)
    return val

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Mean over feasible depths v of candidate i of the number of domain values removed elsewhere by pinning i=v (channel apart/close + census-slot emptying), divided by 4k."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    domf = domain.astype(np.float64)          # (k,4)
    # (a) channel removals for each (i, v)
    # apart: partners j with domain[j,v] -> count 1 each
    apart = (links == 1).astype(np.float64)   # (k,k)
    close = (links == 2).astype(np.float64)   # (k,k)
    # apart_rem[i,v] = sum_j apart[i,j]*domain[j,v]
    apart_rem = apart @ domf                  # (k,4)
    # close: for each j, count w with domain[j,w] and |w-v|>1
    # build per-j "far" counts per v: far[j,v] = sum_w domf[j,w] * [|w-v|>1]
    idx = np.arange(4)
    far_mask = (np.abs(idx[:, None] - idx[None, :]) > 1).astype(np.float64)  # (v,w)
    far = domf @ far_mask.T                   # (k,4): far[j,v]
    close_rem = close @ far                   # (k,4)
    chan_rem = apart_rem + close_rem          # (k,4)
    # (b) census removals: for each v, depths d with census_left[d] - (d==v) == 0
    # count of other candidates j!=i with domain[j,d] true = colsum_d - domain[i,d]
    colsum = domf.sum(axis=0)                 # (4,)
    # census_rem[i,v] = sum_d [census_left[d]-(d==v)==0] * (colsum[d]-domain[i,d])
    cl = census_left.astype(np.float64)       # (4,)
    # indicator matrix ind[v,d]
    ind = (cl[None, :] - (idx[:, None] == idx[None, :]).astype(np.float64) == 0).astype(np.float64)  # (v,d)
    other_counts = colsum[None, :] - domf     # (k,4) over d
    census_rem = other_counts @ ind.T         # (k,4) over v
    total = chan_rem + census_rem             # (k,4)
    feas = domf.sum(axis=1)                   # (k,)
    summed = (total * domf).sum(axis=1)       # (k,)
    denom = np.maximum(feas, 1.0) * (4.0 * k)
    out = np.where(feas > 0, summed / denom, 0.0)
    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Tightest-basin slack pressure weighted by whether the candidate's own removal actually shrinks the basin's reachable range (marginal tightness contribution)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min          # (B,)
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max          # (B,)
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    t = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)      # (B,) tightness

    # Marginal contribution of each candidate to its basins' tightness:
    # if the basin's slack is already 0 (over-constrained), removing a member
    # that spans the full range matters; if slack is large, any member is fine.
    # Contribution = how much the candidate widens the basin's range relative
    # to what the basin needs.
    span = np.maximum(dom_max - dom_min, 0.0)          # (k,)
    # candidate's "range share" in each basin: its span over sum of spans
    span_sum = M.T @ span                               # (B,)
    share = np.where(span_sum[None, :] > 1e-9, span[:, None] / np.maximum(span_sum[None, :], 1e-9), 0.0)  # (k,B)

    # range deficit: how much the basin's remaining range misses the target
    # (target rest_b must sit inside [min_sum, max_sum])
    deficit = np.maximum(basin_rest - max_sum, 0.0) + np.maximum(min_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)  # (B,)
    # relative deficit vs. basin's own remaining reach
    reach = np.maximum(max_sum - min_sum, 1e-9)
    rel_deficit = np.minimum(deficit / reach, 1.0)  # (B,)

    # combined weight per (candidate, basin): tightness scaled by rel_deficit,
    # times candidate's range share (only candidates whose removal hurts matter)
    w = t[None, :] * (1.0 + rel_deficit[None, :]) * (0.25 + share)
    masked = np.where(basins, w, -1.0)
    best = masked.max(axis=1)
    return np.where(basins.any(axis=1), np.clip(best, -1.0, 1.0), 0.0)
features.measures: Tightest-basin slack pressure weighted by whether the candidate's own removal actually shrinks the basin's reachable range (marginal tightness contribution).

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Gap between a basin's remaining total and the sum of its open members' *minimum* feasible depths, expressed as the fraction of the basin's total that is still "unforced"; averaged over the basins a candidate belongs to, 0 if in none. High = the basin can still shrink a lot."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    depths = np.arange(4, dtype=np.float64)

    # smallest feasible depth per candidate (forced floor)
    dom_min = np.where(domain, depths[None, :], np.inf).min(axis=1)  # (k,)

    # sum of open members' min feasible depth per basin
    member_min_sum = basins.T.astype(np.float64) @ dom_min  # (B,)

    # remaining total still to be placed above the floors
    rest = basin_rest.astype(np.float64)
    forced_room = rest - member_min_sum  # (B,): how much still has to come from raising members

    # normalise by the basin's target (so basins of different size are comparable)
    denom = np.maximum(np.abs(rest), 1.0)
    frac = forced_room / denom  # (B,)

    # average over the basins the candidate belongs to
    M = basins.astype(np.float64)
    cnt = np.maximum(M.sum(axis=1), 1.0)
    avg = (M @ frac) / cnt  # (k,)

    out = np.where(basins.any(axis=1), avg, 0.0)
    return np.clip(np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0), -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Min over the candidate's basins of the worst-case (over feasible depths) predicted post-pin census pressure: for each depth, the census deficit weighted by how many other open members of the basin compete for the same scarce depths."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    if basins.shape[1] == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    idx = np.arange(4)
    feas = domain.astype(bool)  # (k,4)

    # scarcity of each depth from the census: rarer remaining slot -> higher
    tot = float(max(census_left.sum(), 1))
    scarcity = (tot - census_left.astype(float)) / tot  # (4,)

    # for each candidate and basin: how competing are the other open members
    B = basins.shape[1]
    bmask = basins.astype(bool)                # (k,B)
    cnt = bmask.sum(axis=0).astype(float)      # (B,) open members per basin
    # competing open members other than i, per candidate-basin
    others = np.maximum(cnt[None, :] - bmask.astype(float), 0.0)  # (k,B)

    # per candidate-basin: sum over other open members of their census-pressure
    # pressure of a member j = sum over its feasible depths of scarcity
    member_pressure = (feas.astype(float) * scarcity[None, :]).sum(axis=1)  # (k,)
    total_other_pressure = (bmask.astype(float) @ member_pressure[None, :].T).ravel() if False else None
    # sum over other open members of basin b (excluding i) of member_pressure
    sum_all = bmask.astype(float).T @ member_pressure  # (B,)
    other_pressure = sum_all[None, :] - bmask.astype(float) * member_pressure[:, None]  # (k,B)

    # normalise by basin size to keep scale in check
    other_pressure = other_pressure / np.maximum(others, 1.0)

    # candidate's own feasible-depth scarcity, per basin
    own_pres = (feas.astype(float) * scarcity[None, :])  # (k,4)

    # For each depth v of candidate i: combined pressure = own + others
    comb = own_pres[:, None, :] + other_pressure[:, :, None]  # (k,B,4)
    comb = np.where(feas[:, None, :], comb, -np.inf)
    worst = comb.max(axis=2)                                    # (k,B) worst over depths
    worst = np.where(bmask, worst, np.inf)                      # only own basins
    val = worst.min(axis=1)                                     # (k,)
    val = np.where(np.isfinite(val), val, 0.0)

    # baseline: candidates whose basins are small get smaller pressure; subtract own
    # normalise into roughly [-1,1] via a soft cap
    return np.clip(val, 0.0, 1.0) - 1.0
features.measures: Min over the candidate's basins of the worst-case (over feasible depths) predicted post-pin census pressure: for each depth, the census deficit weighted by how many other open members of the basin compete for the same scarce depths.

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Per candidate: how much its feasible depths force a channel partner into a small domain, using the partner's restricted-domain size after removing incompatible depths (tightness propagation pressure)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom = domain.astype(np.float64)
    d = np.arange(4)
    diff = np.abs(d[:, None] - d[None, :])  # (4,4)
    apart_ok = (diff > 0).astype(np.float64)
    close_ok = (diff <= 1).astype(np.float64)

    # For each partner j and each depth v the candidate could take: number of
    # remaining depths of j that stay compatible with v.
    comp_apart = dom @ apart_ok.T   # (k,4): depth v -> # j-depths compatible under apart
    comp_close = dom @ close_ok.T   # (k,4)

    apart_mask = (links == 1).astype(np.float64)
    close_mask = (links == 2).astype(np.float64)

    # A candidate depth v is "squeezing" partner j if it leaves j with few options.
    # partner domain size before (per partner)
    psize = dom.sum(axis=1)  # (k,)

    # for each (i,v): sum over partners j of (compatible count) / (partner domain size)
    # -> small value means candidate's depth narrows partners strongly
    per_i_v = apart_mask @ comp_apart + close_mask @ comp_close  # (k,4) raw counts
    npart = (apart_mask.sum(1) + close_mask.sum(1))[:, None]    # (k,1)
    # normalise by partner count and typical partner domain size
    avg_psize = np.maximum((apart_mask + close_mask) @ psize, 1e-6)[:, None]  # (k,1)
    frac = per_i_v / np.maximum(npart, 1.0) / np.maximum(avg_psize, 1.0)      # (k,4) in ~[0,1]

    # candidate's own feasible depths; squeezing = low frac -> pressure = 1 - frac
    pressure = (1.0 - frac) * dom
    # average over candidate's own feasible depths
    own = np.maximum(dom.sum(axis=1), 1.0)
    score = pressure.sum(axis=1) / own  # (k,)

    # no partners -> neutral 0
    has_partner = ((apart_mask + close_mask).sum(1) > 0).astype(np.float64)
    return np.clip(score * has_partner, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Apart-vs-close channel asymmetry: narrowness-weighted shared-depth overlap with apart partners minus that with close partners, each normalised by partner count."""
    domf = domain.astype(float)
    dsize = domf.sum(1)
    apart = (links == 1).astype(float)
    close = (links == 2).astype(float)
    A = apart @ (domf / dsize[:, None])   # (k,4) narrowness-weighted share
    C = close @ (domf / dsize[:, None])
    a = ((A * domf).sum(1) / np.maximum(dsize, 1)) / (1 + apart.sum(1))

    domf = domain.astype(float)
    k = domf.shape[0]

    # min and max feasible depth per candidate
    dmin = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dmax = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)

    hi_all = M.T @ dmax  # (B,)

    lo_oth = lo_all[None, :] - dmin[:, None] * M  # (k, B)
    hi_oth = hi_all[None, :] - dmax[:, None] * M  # (k, B)

    V = np.arange(4)  # (4,)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Sum over a candidate's basins of per-basin slack pressure, where each basin's slack is measured against the domain-restricted reachable window only (counted once per candidate-depth pairing, not just basin max)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min      # (B,)
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max      # (B,)
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    press = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)   # (B,) per-basin pressure in (0,1]

    # Only count basins where the candidate is actually one of the open members
    # driving the constraint: weight by 1/open so tight basins shared by many
    # candidates don't dominate just by membership count.
    open_cnt = np.maximum(basin_open.astype(float), 1.0)  # (B,)
    w = press / open_cnt                                  # (B,)

    in_basin = basins.astype(float)                       # (k,B)
    contrib = in_basin * w[None, :]                       # (k,B)

    # Aggregate: mean over the candidate's basins (0 if none) so a candidate in
    # many loose basins doesn't beat one in a single tight basin.
    n_b = in_basin.sum(axis=1)
    tot = contrib.sum(axis=1)
    out = np.where(n_b > 0, tot / np.maximum(n_b, 1.0), 0.0)

    # Sharpen: emphasise the max single tight basin alongside the mean.
    masked = np.where(basins, press[None, :], -1.0)
    best = masked.max(axis=1)
    best = np.where(basins.any(axis=1), best, 0.0)

    # Combine mean (spread pressure) and max (very tight basin) with a bias to the max.
    return np.clip(0.4 * out + 0.6 * best, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Basin 'bottleneck tightness': for each candidate, the tightest basin it is in, but discounted by how many other tight basins it also shares (multi-constraint pressure)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    dmin = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dmax = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dmin
    max_sum = M.T @ dmax
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    W = slo + shi  # (B,) total slack/overshoot width
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + W)  # (B,)
    mask = basins & (basin_open[None, :] >= 2)
    tight_masked = np.where(mask, tight[None, :], 0.0)  # (k,B)
    best = tight_masked.max(axis=1)  # (k,)
    # number of basins the candidate shares that are at least moderately tight
    share = (tight_masked > 0.2).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    # discount: more shared tight basins -> less unique pressure from the single tightest
    out = best * (1.0 + np.log1p(share)) / 4.0
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """For each candidate: fraction of its feasible depths that leave the basin's residual coverable only by a narrow margin (near-stranding), summed over its basins with tightness weights and a bonus when a depth would pin the basin exactly (bad -> negative)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]

    dom = np.asarray(domain).astype(bool)
    Bmask = np.asarray(basins).astype(bool)

    dom_min = np.argmax(dom, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(dom[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = Bmask.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    slack = slo + shi
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slack)

    others = np.maximum(basin_open.astype(float)[None, :] - M, 0.0)  # (k,B)

    rest_b = basin_rest[None, :, None]
    v = np.arange(4)[None, None, :]
    residual = rest_b - v
    span = 3.0 * others[:, :, None]
    lo = np.maximum(residual - span, 0.0)
    hi = np.minimum(residual, span)
    coverable = (residual >= lo - 1e-9) & (residual <= hi + 1e-9) & (residual >= 0.0)

    center = 1.5 * others[:, :, None]
    margin = np.abs(residual - center) - center
    room = np.maximum(-margin, 0.0)
    near = np.where(coverable, 1.0 / (1.0 + room), 0.0)
    pinned = np.where(coverable & (room < 1e-9), 1.0, 0.0)

    own_feas = dom[:, None, :]
    has_other = (others > 0)[:, :, None]

    risky = own_feas & has_other & coverable & (near > 0.5)
    pin_bonus = own_feas & has_other & (pinned > 0.5)

    dom_size = np.maximum(dom.sum(axis=1), 1).astype(float)
    risk_frac = risky.sum(axis=2).astype(float) / dom_size[:, None]
    pin_frac = pin_bonus.sum(axis=2).astype(float) / dom_size[:, None]

    score_b = (0.6 * risk_frac + 0.4 * pin_frac) * tight[None, :]
    score_b = np.where(Bmask, score_b, 0.0)
    best = score_b.max(axis=1)

    return np.clip(-best, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Per candidate: tightness-weighted count of assigned channel partners it conflicts with, plus a bonus for how many of its feasible depths are blocked by assigned partners (propagation already done)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    dom_size = np.maximum(domain.sum(axis=1), 1).astype(float)

    # For each candidate, estimate how constrained its feasible depths are by channels
    # to already-assigned pools: recompute which depths each assigned partner forbids.
    # We don't have partner domains, but assigned_links tells how many such partners.
    # Use wipeout memory as a proxy for "this candidate keeps getting squeezed".
    w = wipeouts.astype(float)
    wmax = w.max() if k > 0 else 0.0
    wnorm = w / (1.0 + wmax)  # in [0,1)

    # Basin tightness (as elsewhere): tightest basin this candidate sits in
    dmin = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dmax = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - (M.T @ dmin), 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum((M.T @ dmax) - basin_rest, 0.0)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)
    masked = np.where(basins, tight[None, :], 0.0)
    best_tight = masked.max(axis=1)

    # Channel-constrained signal: assigned neighbours squeeze a candidate more when
    # its domain is small relative to how many assigned neighbours it has.
    al = assigned_links.astype(float)
    chan_pressure = al / (1.0 + dom_size)  # more assigned links & smaller domain -> higher

    # Combine: candidate is attractive (high priority) when it's been hit by wipeouts
    # (search wants to test it), OR highly squeezed (branching here resolves tension).
    out = 0.7 * wnorm + 0.5 * best_tight * (1.0 + chan_pressure) - 0.3 * chan_pressure
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Sensitivity of each basin's achievable-total interval to the candidate's own depth: average over the candidate's basins of (interval width after removing the candidate) / (1 + own domain size), so basins whose flexibility collapses without this pool score high."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    dom_min = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dom_max = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    dom_size = domain.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dom_min           # (B,)
    max_sum = M.T @ dom_max           # (B,)
    # width of the total interval achievable by each basin's open members
    width = np.maximum(max_sum - min_sum, 0.0)         # (B,)
    # width with the candidate removed from its basins
    # for each candidate i and basin b it is in: width_b - (dom_max_i - dom_min_i)
    own_span = (dom_max - dom_min)                      # (k,)
    contrib = own_span[:, None] * M                     # (k,B) span removed if i leaves basin b
    width_wo = np.maximum(width[None, :] - contrib, 0.0)  # (k,B)
    # collapse factor: how much of the width is due to the candidate
    denom = np.maximum(width[None, :], 1e-9)
    collapse = np.where(basins, contrib / denom, 0.0)   # (k,B) in [0,1]
    # weight by inverse own domain size: small domain -> this candidate's depth matters more
    w = 1.0 / (1.0 + dom_size)                          # (k,)
    # average collapse over the candidate's basins (0 if none)
    cnt = np.maximum(basins.sum(axis=1), 1).astype(float)
    avg = (collapse.sum(axis=1) / cnt) * w
    return np.clip(avg, 0.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Spread of each candidate's tight-basin slack: tightest-basin tightness minus the average tightness of its other >=2-open basins (positive = one basin dominates its constraints)."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    dmin = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(float)
    dmax = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(float)
    M = basins.astype(float)
    min_sum = M.T @ dmin
    max_sum = M.T @ dmax
    slo = np.maximum(basin_rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - basin_rest, 0.0)
    W = slo + shi                       # (B,)
    tight = 1.0 / (1.0 + W)             # (B,)
    mask = basins & (basin_open[None, :] >= 2)
    tm = np.where(mask, tight[None, :], 0.0)   # (k,B)
    n = mask.sum(axis=1).astype(float)         # (k,) number of tight-basin memberships
    best = tm.max(axis=1)
    total = tm.sum(axis=1)
    # average over the *other* basins (best removed)
    others_mean = np.where(n > 1, (total - best) / np.maximum(n - 1.0, 1.0), 0.0)
    out = np.where(n > 0, best - others_mean, 0.0)
    return np.clip(out, -1.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """For each candidate: fraction of its feasible depths that, if chosen, would exhaust a census slot that a still-open basin depends on as sole provider."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]

    dom_f = domain.astype(float)  # (k,4)
    M = basins.astype(float)     # (k,B)

    # per basin, per depth: how many open members can take that depth
    basin_depth_count = M.T @ dom_f  # (B,4)

    # sole provider: count == 1 for that (basin, depth)
    sole = (basin_depth_count == 1.0)  # (B,4)

    # sole_prov[c,b,v]: candidate c is the sole open provider of depth v in basin b
    # M is (k,B), dom_f is (k,4), sole is (B,4)
    sole_prov = M[:, :, None] * dom_f[:, None, :] * sole[None, :, :]  # (k,B,4)

    census_l = census_left.astype(float)  # (4,)
    exhaust = (census_l <= 1.0)           # (4,)

    basin_needs = (basin_rest > 0)        # (B,)

    # risky[c,b,v]
    risky = sole_prov * basin_needs[None, :, None] * exhaust[None, None, :]  # (k,B,4)

    # per candidate, per depth: is this depth risky in any basin the candidate belongs to?
    risk_per_depth = risky.sum(axis=1) > 0  # (k,4)
    risk_per_depth = risk_per_depth & domain  # only feasible depths count

    n_risk = risk_per_depth.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    dsize = np.maximum(domain.sum(axis=1), 1).astype(float)
    return -np.clip(n_risk / dsize, 0.0, 1.0)

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Decayed sum of a candidate's three tightest basin tightnesses: (t1 + 0.5*t2 + 0.25*t3)/1.75."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    if B == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # lowest / highest feasible depth per candidate
    lo = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(np.float64)          # (k,)
    hi = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(np.float64)  # (k,)

    # basin sums of lowest / highest feasible depths over members
    min_sum = basins.T.astype(np.float64) @ lo                 # (B,)
    max_sum = basins.T.astype(np.float64) @ hi                 # (B,)

    rest = basin_rest.astype(np.float64)
    slo = np.maximum(rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - rest, 0.0)
    T = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)                                # (B,)

    Tm = basins.astype(np.float64) * T[None, :]                # (k, B)
    # sort each row descending
    Ts = -np.sort(-Tm, axis=1)                                 # (k, B) descending

    t1 = Ts[:, 0] if B >= 1 else np.zeros(k)
    t2 = Ts[:, 1] if B >= 2 else np.zeros(k)
    t3 = Ts[:, 2] if B >= 3 else np.zeros(k)

    score = (t1 + 0.5 * t2 + 0.25 * t3) / 1.75
    return score

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):

    mind = dom_size.min()

    # slo/shi: smallest/largest depths still possible for the other open members of the basin.
    # Reconstruct per-basin slo/shi from the candidate domains and basin membership.
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    T = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    if B > 0:
        # For each basin, compute slo/shi over its open members (candidates), excluding each member.
        # depths possible: domain rows; use large sentinels for min/max aggregation.
        depths = np.arange(4, dtype=np.float64)
        # per candidate per basin: min and max feasible depth (only where member)
        # feasible min depth: first True column; max: last True column
        has = domain.any(1)
        first = np.argmax(domain, axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # first True
        last = (3 - np.argmax(domain[:, ::-1], axis=1)).astype(np.float64)  # last True
        member = basins.astype(bool)
        BIG = 1e6
        # basin-level min/max over open members
        bmin = np.full(B, BIG)
        bmax = np.full(B, -BIG)
        for b in range(B):
            m = member[:, b]
            if m.any():
                bmin[b] = first[m].min()
                bmax[b] = last[m].max()
        # per candidate: for each basin it belongs to, slo/shi over the OTHER open members
        # other members = basin members minus this candidate
        for b in range(B):
            m = member[:, b]
            if not m.any():
                continue
            # count of members and their min/max; to exclude one candidate we need
            # the min/max over others. Compute via sorted approach per basin.
            idx = np.where(m)[0]
            f = first[idx]
            l = last[idx]
            # for each member i, min over others and max over others
            # use prefix/suffix or simple: since basin sizes are small (<=6), loop over members
            for j, i in enumerate(idx):
                others = np.ones(len(idx), dtype=bool)
                others[j] = False
                if others.any():
                    slo = f[others].min()
                    shi = l[others].max()
                else:
                    slo = 0.0
                    shi = 0.0
                tb = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)
                if tb > T[i]:

import numpy as np

def feature(domain, links, assigned_links, basins, basin_open, basin_rest, wipeouts, census_left, depth):
    """Power mean (p=6) of basin tightness T=1/(1+slo+shi) over each candidate's member basins, 0 if none."""
    k = domain.shape[0]
    B = basins.shape[1]
    if B == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # feasible depth extremes per candidate (columns 0..3)
    idx = np.arange(4)[None, :]
    big = 10
    lo = np.where(domain, idx, big).min(axis=1)          # (k,)
    hi = np.where(domain, idx, -big).max(axis=1)         # (k,)
    lo = np.where(domain.any(axis=1), lo, 0)
    hi = np.where(domain.any(axis=1), hi, 0)

    bmask = basins.astype(bool)                          # (k, B)
    openf = bmask.astype(np.float64)                     # (k, B)
    # min_sum / max_sum over open members of each basin
    min_sum = openf.T @ lo.astype(np.float64)            # (B,)
    max_sum = openf.T @ hi.astype(np.float64)            # (B,)

    rest = basin_rest.astype(np.float64)                 # (B,)
    slo = np.maximum(rest - min_sum, 0.0)
    shi = np.maximum(max_sum - rest, 0.0)
    T = 1.0 / (1.0 + slo + shi)                          # (B,)

    T6 = T ** 6
    num = openf @ T6                                     # (k,)
    den = openf.sum(axis=1)                              # (k,)
    safe_den = np.maximum(den, 1.0)
    score = np.where(den > 0, (num / safe_den) ** (1.0 / 6.0), 0.0)
    return np.clip(score, 0.0, 1.0)

nodes.title: sparsity-conditional-channel-gate
nodes.description: A conditional score that fires only when the candidate's tightest basin is loose or absent, then ranking by channel-degree/domain interaction, so it switches on in the sparse scatter/strip regime.

nodes.title: census-feasibility-lookahead
nodes.description: For each candidate, the number of its feasible depths that leave the remaining census satisfiable (Hall condition over the 16 depth subsets); prefer few, i.e. the census nearly forces the branch.

nodes.title: wide find: basin_residual_reachability_fraction
nodes.description: For each candidate: the fraction of its feasible depths that would, if chosen, complete a basin exactly (that basin's open count would drop to zero and the residual total would be met), weighted by t…

nodes.title: basin-slack-gradient-per-depth
nodes.description: For each candidate depth, the reduction in the tightest basin's slack if that depth is taken, so the branch that most constrains the basin is preferred.

nodes.title: basin-forced-bill
nodes.description: For each candidate, the largest minimal per-depth spend its tightest basin forces on the remaining open members, a bolder form of tightness.

nodes.title: channel-basin-cross-pressure
nodes.description: Combine a candidate's channel-degree scarcity with the tightness of the basins its channel partners sit in, so pivotal neighbours are preferred.

nodes.title: wide find: channel_partner_breadth_reduction
nodes.description: For each candidate: how much assigning it reduces the total remaining search breadth, measured as the census-slot scarcity-weighted entropy drop of its channel partners' domains.

nodes.title: basin-forced-value-detection
nodes.description: Prefer candidates whose basin, given remaining slack, forces a specific depth value on them (slack equals a single feasible depth).

nodes.title: basin-partner-stranding-sync
nodes.description: For each candidate, how many of its basin co-open partners would be stranded to a single depth if the candidate took each feasible depth, weighted by partner tightness.

nodes.title: basin-free-fallback
nodes.description: For candidates in no basin (or only loose basins), rank by channel-degree and domain narrowness so they are not left at zero by the dominant basin features.

nodes.title: census-stranding-lookahead
nodes.description: For each candidate depth, whether taking it would leave some depth's census count unsatisfiable given the remaining pools' domains (a Hall-style check on the census alone).

nodes.title: channel-spread-strip
nodes.description: Prefer candidates whose unassigned channel partners are spread along the strip axis (high positional variance), so branching splits the search rather than clustering it.

nodes.title: wide find: singleton_partner_channel_consistency
nodes.description: For each candidate: count of its channel partners whose current domain is a singleton strictly inside this candidate's range-adjacency — measures propagation depth through chains, normalised by partn…

nodes.title: per-depth-domain-reduction
nodes.description: For each candidate depth, the total number of domain values removed from all other candidates by one-step propagation, so the branch that prunes the most is preferred.

nodes.title: census-basin-feasible-depth-count
nodes.description: Per candidate, count how many of its feasible depths keep every basin it touches and the census jointly satisfiable, a joint feasibility gate.

nodes.title: size-conditional-gate
nodes.description: A feature that switches on only when the search is large (depth relative to n), targeting growth with puzzle size in strip and scatter.

nodes.title: wide find: basin_depth_entropy_deficit
nodes.description: Per candidate: the reduction in total basin-domain entropy (over depths) that branching on it would produce, weighted by basin tightness; high when the candidate is the most entropy-reducing hinge of…

nodes.title: channel-type-asymmetry
nodes.description: Separate `apart` from `close` channels: prefer candidates with many unresolved `apart` partners whose domains still overlap, since apart constraints propagate hardest and no kept feature tells the two channel types apart.

nodes.title: basin-co-membership-reach
nodes.description: For each candidate, how many other open pools share at least one of its basins, weighted by those basins' tightness, i.e. how much of the remaining search mass its basins touch.

nodes.title: wide find: channel_partner_squeeze_pressure
nodes.description: Per candidate: how much its feasible depths force a channel partner into a small domain, using the partner's restricted-domain size after removing incompatible depths (tightness propagation pressure).

nodes.title: basin-tightness-third-order
nodes.description: Aggregate tightness across a candidate's three tightest basins with decaying weights, so multi-basin pools dominate.

nodes.title: mrv-basin-tightness-joint
nodes.description: Rank by small domain size scaled by the tightness of the candidate's tightest basin, so narrow pools inside tight basins come first.

nodes.title: census-scarcity-basin-open-weighted
nodes.description: Census scarcity of a candidate's feasible depths weighted by how many open basin partners share those depths.

nodes.title: wide find: wipeout_and_channel_pressure
nodes.description: Per candidate: tightness-weighted count of assigned channel partners it conflicts with, plus a bonus for how many of its feasible depths are blocked by assigned partners (propagation already done).

nodes.title: wide find: sole_provider_census_exhaustion_risk
nodes.description: For each candidate: fraction of its feasible depths that, if chosen, would exhaust a census slot that a still-open basin depends on as sole provider.
